focus_areas: Skin texture realism (specular highlights vs. plastic look)
Boundary integrity between subject and complex background
Anatomical correctness of visible limbs and tail proportion
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'wetness' of the skin. AI often fails to render the specific type of specular highlight found on amphibian mucous membranes, resulting in either a dry matte look or an overly uniform plastic shine. Also, scrutinize the transition between the yellow markings and the black skin; in real salamanders, this boundary is sharp but organic, whereas AI may show bleeding or haloing. Check if the background leaves have coherent 3D structure or if they collapse into a flat texture map near the subject.
image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a European fire salamander (Salamandra salamandra) resting on a bed of dark, decaying leaf litter. The salamander has a glossy black body with distinct, irregular yellow-orange markings along its back and head. Its skin appears wet and textured. The head is visible on the left, showing a broad shape, while the body curves towards the right, ending in a tail that blends slightly with the background leaves.

expert_testimonies.reason: To confirm the salamander is physically resting ON the leaves (correct occlusion/depth) and not floating or merged.
Primary verification of species identity and coloration patterns against ImageNet classes.
To verify the continuity of the salamander's form and ensure no limbs or tail segments are fused with the background leaves.
To assess the realism of the skin texture (glossiness) and detect subtle noise or smoothing artifacts in the background.

evidence.thinking_trajectory: The image appears to be clear and well-defined, but there are no visible signs of noise, compression, blur, or darken. The colors are vibrant, and the details on the salamander's skin texture are sharp. The image seems to have a slight graininess that could suggest a minor level of noise, but this is not prominent.
